name: How much value does an island add to a remodel?

mainEntity.name: Does adding a kitchen island during a remodel actually improve function enough to be worth the cost?
mainEntity.text: Does adding a kitchen island during a remodel actually improve function enough to be worth the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen island is valuable only when the room has enough clearance to use it well. In a properly sized kitchen, an island can add prep space, storage, seating, a work zone for cooking or cleanup, and a stronger sense of organization. But if the kitchen is too narrow, the island can block movement, create pinch points, and make appliances harder to use. That is why layout planning matters more than simply adding features. Homeowners should evaluate walkways, appliance door swings, and the relationship between the sink, range, and refrigerator. In many Los Angeles homes, an island is one of the most requested upgrades, but it should be sized for circulation first and style second.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen island can improve storage, prep space, seating, and traffic flow if the kitchen is large enough to support it. If clearance is too tight, an island can make the room feel cramped and reduce function instead of improving it.
